SECANT PILING

Why Secant Pile Installation Records Matter to Project Owners

Turn construction records into useful evidence for review, handover and future enquiries.

In this insight

Records connect intent and executionAgree the record structure earlyMake exceptions easy to findPlan the handover around future useFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Records connect intent and execution

A drawing describes what is intended; an installation record describes what was reported during construction. For a secant wall, the project team needs a consistent way to connect each pile identifier with its location, installation information and associated inspection evidence. The exact record requirements should come from the approved specification. Owners benefit when this information is planned before work starts rather than reconstructed at completion.

Agree the record structure early

Ask the designer and contractor to agree a common naming system, drawing revision reference and submission format. Define who creates the record, who checks it and how queries are closed. A spreadsheet may be sufficient if its fields are controlled and its links are reliable. A sophisticated platform cannot compensate for missing identifiers, incompatible revisions or undocumented changes in the field.

Make exceptions easy to find

A useful dashboard should distinguish completed records from records awaiting review and records with unresolved exceptions. Do not let a high completion percentage hide a small number of significant issues. Give each exception an owner and a documented response. The commercial value comes from reducing ambiguity at interfaces, particularly before excavation exposes work that was previously below ground.

Plan the handover around future use

The final package should be searchable by location and understandable to someone who did not attend daily site meetings. Include the agreed as-built information, approval history and close-out documents. Retain original records when preparing summaries so the source remains available. This does not turn paperwork into a guarantee of performance; it provides a traceable basis for technical assessment, asset management and future alterations.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Agree identifiers before installation begins.
  • Track unresolved exceptions separately.
  • Deliver searchable records with their source evidence.
